mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% within a month signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS decreases by more than 0.25% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month indicates strengthening consumer demand, which typically boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances where RSAFS increases by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals economic weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) over three consecutive months signals a weakening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO declines for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% month-over-month signals a strengthening housing market, which typically boosts related sectors and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where HOUST increases by more than 5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals inflationary pressure during a tightening cycle, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) for three consecutive months signals a strengthening labor market, which typically boosts consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances where PAYEMS increases for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) grows by less than 1% quarter-over-quarter and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) increases by more than 0.3% within the same period, it signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth < 1% QoQ and UNRATE increases > 0.3% in 1 quarter
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where GDPC1 grows by less than 1% QoQ and UNRATE increases by more than 0.3% within the same period.
